# Part 3 source records: close works named by the Codex survey and the deck that the store lacked

**Date:** 2026-09-29 · generated by `tools/evidence-check/build_part3_files.py` from the verified store; not edited by hand.

Each work was saved as full text and read by one agent, which locked every item to a line of the saved text with a short verbatim anchor. A script checked that each anchor occurs in the saved text and that the numbers of the item stand within three lines of it. A second agent, which did not write the record, then tried to refute each item against the text. Items shown here passed both checks. Where the auditor corrected an item, the corrected wording is shown and the Audit column says so. The verbatim anchors and the saved texts are kept outside the repository; this file gives the location of every item instead. Only works that are eligible under the source rule of 2026-09-29 (D313) are listed; the others are in the evidence ledger, section 1b.

Columns: # = item index (the reference is <record id>#<index>); Field = what the item is about; Line = line in the saved text of the version read. Full references: evidence ledger, References.

| 0 | what_is_changed | What learning changes is an external per-app memory: a transition graph holding (i) the sub-tasks available on each app screen (Explore), (ii) the sequence of sub-tasks of each task (Select), and (iii) how to perform each sub-task (Derive). Graphs exist per app, not per task, so all tasks of an app share one graph. | - | Design description, no measurement. | Sec. 4.1 Memory Structure | 192 | primary | supported |
| 1 | selection_rule | After MobileGPT completes the user instruction (the Select phase indicates full execution, i.e. the LLM selects the global sub-task 'Finish'), it stores the task as a collection of (page node, sub-task) pairs, so a recalled task bypasses Explore, Select and Derive and can start from whatever page the app is on. In the ablation, tasks marked as failed are repaired with HITL repair and the repaired path is what is stored (Sec. 7.3.1, line 323). | - | Design description, no measurement. Completion trigger: Select phase indicating the instruction is fully executed (Sec. 2.1, line 128; Sec. 3.2, line 172: LLM selects 'Finish'). | 2 | mechanism | Reuse adapts stored actions by reversing the storage-time generalization: stored actions keep the target UI's key attributes with parameter-valued attributes replaced by parameter names (Sec. 5.1, line 220); on recall the LLM slot-fills the sub-task parameters (line 231), MobileGPT substitutes the new values and finds the UI element that matches the updated attributes. | - | Design description (attribute-based action adaptation), no measurement. | Sec. 5.1 Attribute-based Action Adaptation, 'Adapting Actions' | 232 | primary | supported |
| 3 | proposal_method | Memory content is proposed by the LLM from dedicated offline exploration: before any task, a random explorer and a user trace monitor visit app screens and, for each visited screen, the LLM generates the list of available sub-tasks, which is cached for the Select phase; screens not explored offline are analysed on demand during task execution. | - | Design description, no measurement. | Sec. 2.1 System Workflow, 'Explore' | 123 | primary | supported |
| 4 | signal | The automatic error signal is a hand-written rule set: the authors heuristically identified two common error types and built a rule-based self-feedback module that appends feedback to the next prompt when an error is detected (line 178: invalid or non-clickable UI index; no screen change or looping over the same screens). The paper describes no automatic answer key or ground-truth reward; beyond these rules, errors are corrected by optional human (HITL) repair, whose corrected actions are stored and later used as correct few-shot examples (Sec. 5.2, lines 243-244). | - | Design description, no measurement. | Sec. 3.3 Dual Strategy Failure Handling, 'Self-Correcting through feedback generation' | 177 | primary | corrected by the auditor |
